title: The long-term divergence exponent and the temporal structure of step-to-step perturbations: a simulation study in two passive walking models
html:
Abstract:Purpose. Divergence exponents are used to assess the local dynamic stability of gait. Human experiments have related the long-term exponent ($\lambda_L$) to the complexity of gait fluctuations. Model studies used perturbations without controlled temporal structure. The question was whether $\lambda_L$ responds to the temporal structure of perturbations in walkers without neuromuscular control. Methods. Two passive walkers, M1 (pilot) and M2 (exploratory), received step-to-step perturbations of five amplitudes ($\sigma$) and nine temporal structures (ARFIMA parameter $d$), and human stride series of free and metronome walking. Results. At constant amplitude, $\lambda_L$ increased with $d$ in both models. It was higher with free series than with metronome series or with surrogates. It did not follow $\sigma$ in M1 and followed $\sigma$ in M2. Its double dissociation from the short-term exponent was supported in M1 only. In a descriptive analysis, the condition means of $\lambda_L$ correlated with the scaling exponent of the step durations ($r = 0.980$ in M1 and 0.906 in M2). Conclusion. In two passive walkers with fixed mechanics, $\lambda_L$ followed the temporal structure of the perturbations; its specificity depended on the model. This response supports the name attractor complexity index (ACI), proposed for $\lambda_L$ from human experiments.
